questions.q: What does remote work give employees, according to the summary?
a: Freedom to handle life without asking permission
Higher salaries than office jobs
Guaranteed promotions over time
Fewer responsibilities at home
questions.why: Lesson 1 says remote workers can handle school runs and appointments without seeking approval.

questions.q: Why does the summary say offices reduce productivity?
a: Meetings, interruptions and waiting eat up the day
Employees take longer lunch breaks there
Office internet connections are usually slower
Managers watch workers far too closely
questions.why: Lesson 2 says people are surrounded by distractions and often wait on others to proceed.

questions.q: What can managers judge more clearly when work goes remote?
a: The quality of the work itself
How many hours people sit at desks
How friendly employees are to colleagues
Whether people arrive on time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says remote work pushes aside distorting factors and lets output speak for itself.

questions.q: How does Basecamp help remote staff connect?
a: A virtual room for lunch and coffee chats
Weekly mandatory video meetings
A shared vacation calendar
A rotating office schedule
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes a virtual meeting room where employees can share breaks together.

questions.q: What does Basecamp do twice a year for its team?
a: Bring everyone together for an in-person retreat
Rotate employees between regional offices
Close the company for a long holiday
Publish a report on everyone's salary
questions.why: Lesson 3 says two annual retreats let the whole company meet face to face.
